source_refs.note: 4. Steroid Hormones: a main subheading of 16.1.1 Chemical Nature of Hormones, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 59-59.

blocks.text: These hormones are derived from cholesterol (a type of lipid). Unlike proteins, steroids are lipid-soluble (fat-soluble). This means they can move through the cell membrane to give instructions directly to the nucleus. Examples include;

blocks.caption: Steroid hormones
rows: Regulates metabolism and helps the body respond to stress.
Helps the kidneys manage salt and water balance.
Regulates male reproductive tissues and traits.
Regulate the female reproductive system and cycle.
